_note: SAMPLE deal memos (fictional). Each has 'profile' = what the fund knew at decision time (used as input for the backtest) and 'reasoning' = why the partners decided. Replace with the real memos in the same shape.

memos.profile: Bharat Bills digitises invoice discounting for MSME suppliers to large corporates. Founder spent 8 years in trade finance at a private bank. 25 suppliers live in pilot, INR 1.4 Cr monthly invoices financed through bank partners; no balance sheet risk. Raised INR 30 L from angels.
memos.reasoning: Founder-market fit is exceptional - she ran the exact desk this replaces. Pilot shows real pull. Capital light because banks fund the book. We invested because founder insight plus early proof outweighed a crowded category. Outcome: raised seed 14 months later.

memos.profile: Anvil Materials makes low-carbon cement additives. Founders are IIT Bombay PhDs with 3 patents. Lab results show 20% clinker reduction. LOIs from 2 regional cement makers. Grant funded so far.
memos.reasoning: Deeptech where the science is proven at lab scale and buyers have signed LOIs. We accept no revenue at pre-seed in deeptech if the technical risk is retired and a buyer is named. Small cheque gets them to a pilot plant.

memos.profile: Nook Snacks makes millet-based snacks for kids. Founder was category manager at a snacks major for 5 years. INR 12 L monthly GMV, 31% repeat within 60 days, contribution margin positive. Raised INR 50 L.
memos.reasoning: We back consumer brands only with repeat-purchase evidence; 31% repeat at month 6 is strong. Founder knows distribution. Invested.

memos.profile: Saathi Health is a WhatsApp-first chronic care companion for diabetics in tier-2 cities. Founders are a doctor and an ex-product manager from a health app. 8,000 users, 45% monthly retention, launched 4 months ago with a tiny team.
memos.reasoning: Speed of execution impressed us: live in 6 weeks, iterating weekly. Retention is unusual for health. Market is large and under-served. Invested despite no revenue yet.

memos.profile: Kaam Kart is a hyperlocal jobs marketplace for blue-collar workers. Founders are two first-time founders from a consulting firm. 5,000 workers signed up, 40 employers, no repeat hiring data yet.
memos.reasoning: We invested on market size and founder energy. In hindsight founder-market fit was weak; the company shut down after 18 months. Lesson: do not let market size compensate for missing founder-market fit.

memos.profile: AdNinja calls itself an AI marketing platform. Revenue INR 15 L a month, all from managed campaigns delivered by a 20-person team. Plans to build a self-serve product later.
memos.reasoning: This is an agency. Services revenue does not show product pull and does not scale like software. Pass.

memos.profile: Glow Theory is a D2C makeup brand. INR 20 L monthly GMV in 4 months, 80% from paid ads. Founder is a beauty influencer with 400k followers. Repeat rate not tracked.
memos.reasoning: Passed: no repeat data and acquisition is all paid. Note: Glow Theory raised a seed from another fund 10 months later with 28% repeat. We may have been too early to pass; we should have asked for repeat data instead of passing.

memos.profile: Ledgerly is accounting software for SMEs. Raised a USD 2M seed round. 400 paying SMEs.
memos.reasoning: Outside our stage - already raised a priced seed. Pass on stage, not on quality.
